SEC27A-01.note: Two independent clauses (grower moved...; a sheltered block...flowered...) need a semicolon. Comma reads as an appositive renaming 'the orchard' until 'flowered' arrives, making A a strong comma-splice lure; colon fails because the second clause does not explain the first.

SEC27A-02.note: Subject is singular 'milk'; present tense is fixed by the habitual 'unless ... comes back'. Plural lures 'cows'' and past lure from 'injected'.

SEC27A-03.resolving_word_after_blank: British-style ellipsis after main-verb 'have' ('rarely have') is not standard edited American English
SEC27A-03.note: Cataphoric ellipsis: the pro-form stands for 'have trouble', and American English substitutes 'do' for main-verb have; plural 'samples' gives 'do'. 'rarely have' attracts by echoing 'has trouble'; it is British-style object ellipsis after main-verb have, not edited American English.

SEC27A-04.note: Two independent clauses (organizers worried...; a booster...turned out to raise...) need a sentence break. Comma lures as an appositive for 'the last dose' until 'turned out'; colon fails as the second clause is a reversal, not an explanation.

SEC27A-05.note: Plural 'probes' plus duration 'for nine growing seasons' requires present perfect progressive; 'are measuring' is plural but wrong with the duration phrase.

SEC27A-06.note: Compound subject (veterinarian and technicians) takes 'have'; 'their' refers to the birds. 'its' lures via 'flock'/'grower' but has no sensible singular antecedent.

SEC27A-07.note: 'Certain species' (no article) is plural; present tense from 'as long as a bed is not planted'. 'marigold'/'row' singular and 'sowed' past are lures.

SEC27A-08.note: 'found [that] the bottles ... were used' takes a noun-clause object with no punctuation. Garden path: 'found the hand-rub bottles' reads as a simple object, inviting a break before 'the'.

SEC27A-09.note: Elliptical 'usually is [dependable]' must echo the copula in the main clause ('are ... dependable'); 'do' cannot stand in for 'be'. Singular 'program'.

SEC27A-10.note: Singular possessive: 'the final join of a long career' identifies one propagator. Plural possessive lures from 'propagators' in the first sentence.

SEC27B-01.note: Restrictive participle: the next sentence contrasts these specimens with those from the frozen interior, so 'gathered where...' identifies which specimens; a comma or dash would make it nonrestrictive (all specimens). D is a fragment.

SEC27B-02.note: Plural 'readings'; past tense since the landing stage is long demolished. Singular lures 'harbor'/'pier'; present lure from 'hold'.

SEC27B-03.note: 'marks the first time that' (present) takes present perfect; singular 'bank' not 'bays'. 'was superseded' is the strongest lure (colloquial 'first time I saw').

SEC27B-04.note: 'has always ... subsided' (present perfect active, singular 'level'); 'is always subsided' is a passive of an intransitive. Resolving verb 'subsided' sits well after the blank; 'borehole'/'level' singular, 'charts' plural lure.

SEC27B-05.note: An earthquake has one epicenter, so the participial phrase is nonrestrictive and takes a comma. No-comma A is the strongest lure; the period makes a fragment, colon is unmotivated.

SEC27B-06.note: Singular 'dish' takes 'is swung'; agent is the motors (no one motor suffices), so 'them'. 'it' lures from 'frame'/'reflector'.

SEC27B-07.note: Singular 'drive' (not 'prisms'); past because the duty is obsolete after automation.

SEC27B-08.note: Subject is plural noun 'surges' ('overflow' is a modifier), not verb; present perfect because the result (foundation sits under deep water) holds now. Singular 'has carved' lures readers who parse 'overflow' as subject.

SEC27B-09.note: Plural 'wires', past to match 'wedged', and 'were ... brittle' needs a linking verb; 'have also brittle' is ungrammatical once the interrupter is skipped.

SEC27B-10.note: Name 'Kittiwake Star' follows 'ship' as an appositive; the dash opens a pair the later comma cannot close, the period leaves a fragment, D splits the name. (Strictly a one-ship institute would want a nonrestrictive comma, which is not offered.)

SEC27C-01.note: 'played' is intransitive; 'the pipes mounted highest...' is the main subject, so the comma follows 'played'. Classic garden path: 'played the pipes' reads as verb-object.

SEC27C-02.note: Singular 'portrait', present habitual from 'whenever ... crowd'. Past lure from 'began admitting last spring', plural lures 'donors''/'groups'.

SEC27C-03.note: Plural 'bronzes' with 'since the museum opened' requires present perfect. Singular lures 'collector's'/'temple'.

SEC27C-04.note: 'then a second mask' is a verbless continuation of the prepositional phrase, so a comma; semicolon and colon need an independent clause / explanation.

SEC27C-05.note: Plural 'copies' takes 'follow'; the object is the single psalter, so 'it'. 'follows' lures from 'psalter'.

SEC27C-06.note: Singular 'helper', past progressive interrupted by 'caught fire'. Plural lure 'projectionists''.

SEC27C-07.note: Plural 'tracks'; simple past because of the specific past time 'on the night of the club's closing concert'. Present perfect lures from 'have circulated ... since' in the relative clause.

SEC27C-08.note: Compound subject 'warden ... and his clerk' is plural; 'recording' needs progressive 'are'. 'do recording' is ungrammatical, but 'recording' lies well beyond the blank. A singular parse ('warden chosen by the members and his clerk') would license 'is', but a warden chosen by his own clerk is implausible, so not defensible.

SEC27C-09.note: 'proofread the sheet' is verb-object and the comma closes the introductory clause before the main subject 'pressmen'. A misplaces the comma (leaving 'the sheet pressmen'); B runs the clauses together.

SEC27C-10.note: 'chart' is the main verb; 'historians chart' agrees. 'historian chart' fails agreement; possessives turn 'chart' into a noun and leave no verb.

SEC27D-01.note: A complete clause introduces a three-item list of examples, so a colon; a comma before a comma-separated list blurs the appositive; semicolon needs an IC.

SEC27D-03.note: Plural 'cashiers'; past progressive for the finished paper-ticket years. 'have been logging' fails because the practice ended.

SEC27D-04.note: Elliptical 'have [crept upward] too' must echo the perfect auxiliary 'has crept'; plural 'hours'. 'are too' lures as a bare plural copula; singular lure 'outlet'.

SEC27D-05.note: Phrasal verb 'ruled out' takes the gerund object directly; any mark separates verb from object. Semicolon leaves a fragment.

SEC27D-06.note: Singular 'registrar'; 'it' = the family's questionnaire, not 'answers'. Past fits the audit narrative.

SEC27D-07.note: Singular 'turnout' (not renters/blocks); simple past for 'the mayoral runoff that autumn'.

SEC27D-09.note: The IC is followed by a verbless elaboration, so a colon; semicolon needs an IC. C misplaces the comma and A runs words together.

SEC27D-10.note: Plural possessive: the tally has columns written by different contractors ('the contractor who had written the lower figure'). The cue is two sentences later, so singular 'contractor's' is the strong lure.

tells: The dash is never the key: offered in SEC27A-08, SEC27B-01, SEC27B-10, SEC27D-05 and loses every time.
The semicolon is the key once (SEC27A-01) but loses in SEC27A-08, SEC27C-04, SEC27C-09, SEC27D-01, SEC27D-05, SEC27D-09; mostly a safe elimination.
In punctuation items the no-punctuation option wins 4 times (SEC27A-08, SEC27B-01, SEC27B-10, SEC27D-05) - balanced against comma/colon/semicolon/period keys, no strong letter or shape tell.

Verb items frequently pair a distant tense anchor with a nearby singular/plural lure noun; once a solver learns 'find the head noun, then look for the far tense clue' it works across ~20 items, but that is the rule, not a tell.
